obtainOrConfirmBeforeFiling.obtainedFrom: Louisiana State Police (Right to Review) or the parish sheriff
obtainOrConfirmBeforeFiling.description: Obtain Louisiana criminal background check dated within the past sixty days. Louisiana State Police recommends a fingerprint-based Right to Review, because the motion must match the state rap sheet on arrest and booking date, original arrest charge, arrest number and counts. Order it so it is still inside its sixty-day life on the day the motion is filed; the Article 989 form marks it required on its face.

obtainOrConfirmBeforeFiling.obtainedFrom: The district attorney's office for the parish of conviction
obtainOrConfirmBeforeFiling.description: Obtain District attorney certification verifying no felony convictions during the five-year period and no pending felony charges under a bill of information or indictment. Article 977(A)(2) requires this certification to be included with the motion, and the Article 989 attachment checklist lists it. Ask the district attorney's office in writing; the packet includes a cover request that names the exact certification and the five-year window. LegalEase cannot produce it — it is the district attorney's own statement about their records — and its absence is a filing requirement, not a reason to withhold the packet.

obtainOrConfirmBeforeFiling.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court that signed the order
obtainOrConfirmBeforeFiling.description: Obtain Certified copy of the Article 894(B) order setting aside the conviction and dismissing the prosecution. Ask the clerk for a certified copy of the order of dismissal. Where no such order exists and Article 894 relief appears available, obtain it first through the separate Article 987 set-aside track, then return to this one.

Check your answer to "Has a court already signed an order setting aside the conviction and dismissing the prosecution under Article 894(B)?" against Certified copy of the Article 894(B) order setting aside the conviction and dismissing the prosecution, and correct the packet if they disagree.

obtainOrConfirmBeforeFiling.obtainedFrom: The district attorney's office for the parish
obtainOrConfirmBeforeFiling.description: Obtain Returned Article 988 Motion for Fee Exemption, completed and signed by the district attorney. The packet gives you the Article 988 form with your own fields filled in. Take or send it to the district attorney's office BEFORE the motion is filed. The district attorney or a designee completes the certification boxes and signs, and returns it within fifteen days. Append it to the motion at filing only if you are found eligible. Filing without it means paying the fee, and Article 983 makes the fee non-refundable even if the motion is denied.

obtainOrConfirmBeforeFiling.obtainedFrom: Clerk of court for the parish
obtainOrConfirmBeforeFiling.description: Obtain Bill of information or indictment for each charge. Ask the clerk of court in the parish of arrest or conviction for a copy of the bill of information or indictment for each charge on the arrest.

obtainOrConfirmBeforeFiling.obtainedFrom: Clerk of court for the parish
obtainOrConfirmBeforeFiling.description: Obtain Minute entry showing the final disposition. Ask the clerk of court for the minute entry that shows how each charge was finally disposed of.

obtainOrConfirmBeforeFiling.obtainedFrom: Department of Public Safety and Corrections, Office of Motor Vehicles
obtainOrConfirmBeforeFiling.description: Obtain Certified letter from the Office of Motor Vehicles under Article 984. Article 984 requires a person convicted of operating a vehicle while intoxicated to supplement the motion with a certified letter from the Office of Motor Vehicles proving compliance with that Article, and it is attached to the motion. A further fifty-dollar court cost is assessed and paid to the Office of Motor Vehicles for storage and retrieval.

obtainOrConfirmBeforeFiling.obtainedFrom: The district attorney's office for the parish
obtainOrConfirmBeforeFiling.description: Obtain District attorney certification letter verifying no participation in a pretrial diversion programme. Listed on the Article 989 attachment checklist. Ask the district attorney's office in writing.

obtainOrConfirmBeforeFiling.obtainedFrom: The district attorney, the Louisiana Bureau of Criminal Identification and Information and the arresting law-enforcement agency
obtainOrConfirmBeforeFiling.description: Obtain Affidavit of No Opposition from each named agency. The agencies' own instrument on the Article 990 form. If each named agency executes one and they are attached to the motion, the Article 991 Order provides that no contradictory hearing is required. LegalEase cannot prepare, complete or sign it.
Every finding, ruling, date, place and signature on the Article 991 Order — Article 991 Order — the ordering paragraphs, the date and place line and the judge's signature line.

Every granting or denying paragraph, finding, date, place and signature on the Article 992 Order of Expungement — Article 992 Order of Expungement — the decretal paragraphs, the date and place line and the judge's signature line.
Race and gender — Article 989 Motion, Part I Defendant Information.
The participant's signature and the date of signing — Article 989 Motion, unrepresented-mover signature block on the final page.
Every certification box and the district attorney's signature on the Article 988 Motion for Fee Exemption — Article 988 Motion for Fee Exemption, the certification section and signature block.
The whole of the Article 990 Affidavit of Response — Not printed in the participant packet; described in the filing instructions only.
The clerk's service of the motion and of the order and judgment — Not printed in the participant packet; described in the filing instructions only.
The mover signs the Article 989 Motion in the block headed 'If not represented by counsel'. LegalEase leaves the signature and date blank.

Article 983(A) caps the total cost at five hundred fifty dollars, collected by the clerk at filing and non-refundable even if the motion is denied. Where the conviction is for operating a vehicle while intoxicated, Article 984(C) assesses a further fifty-dollar court cost payable to the Office of Motor Vehicles.

Article 983(F) through the Article 988 Motion for Fee Exemption, but its grounds are non-conviction grounds, so it is rarely available on a conviction track. Louisiana State Police states that a person is ineligible for the exemption if they have ever been convicted of a felony, including an expunged felony.
